reviewFindings.title: Preserve the AbortSignal when draining queued requests
reviewFindings.body: The new signal is stored on the task, but `drain()` still calls `execute({ input: task.input }, transport)`, discarding it. Since queued execution is the default, submitting an already-aborted signal and then draining still invokes transport instead of rejecting; aborting a started queued request also cannot reach transport. Pass the complete task through the drain adapter so both entrypoints use the new worker behavior.

result.solutionAssessment: No, not as submitted. The shared worker is an appropriate owner for the pre-execution check and signal forwarding, but the queue adapter prevents it from receiving the signal. Preserving the task completes the design without new cancellation machinery.
